title: PIIE mourns the passing of beloved colleague, Gary Clyde Hufbauer
gist: Adam Posen's PIIE obituary for Gary Clyde Hufbauer, who died on November 4, 2026. It recalls Hufbauer's part in building PIIE alongside C. Fred Bergsten, his research on trade, tariffs, NAFTA, sanctions and corporate tax, and his final paper with Kate Hetrick on Trump's tariff reversals, published October 27.

insights.claim: Gary Clyde Hufbauer, a cornerstone senior fellow of the Peterson Institute for International Economics, died on November 4, 2026, which PIIE president Adam Posen calls an enormous loss to the field of international economics.
insights.speaker: Adam S. Posen
insights.so_what: PIIE loses one of its most-cited trade and sanctions voices, so expect fewer Hufbauer-branded tariff and sanctions estimates in policy debates.

insights.so_what: Helps explain PIIE's long-standing institutional stance in favor of open trade.

insights.claim: Hufbauer's pioneering research covered international trade, tariffs, free trade agreements (including NAFTA work with Jeffrey J. Schott), economic sanctions and corporate taxation, and it influenced generations of scholars and policymakers.
insights.speaker: Adam S. Posen
insights.so_what: His frameworks on sanctions and FTAs remain standard references when judging the cost of trade and sanctions policy.
insights.quote: His pioneering work on international trade, tariffs, free trade agreements (notably work on NAFTA with Jeffrey J. Schott), economic sanctions, corporate taxation and so much more

insights.claim: Hufbauer kept researching and publishing until his death: his last PIIE analysis, written with Kate Hetrick on Trump's tariff reversals, came out on October 27, 2026, eight days before he died.
insights.speaker: Adam S. Posen
insights.so_what: His final paper on Trump's tariff reversals is a recent PIIE reference point for tracking US tariff policy.

insights.claim: Posen describes Hufbauer as the embodiment of PIIE's values of intellectual engagement, independence and collegiality, and says his 'coaching tree' of research assistants who went on to strong careers is legendary.
insights.speaker: Adam S. Posen
insights.so_what: Many current trade-policy analysts trained under Hufbauer, which keeps his methods in use.
insights.quote: His coaching tree of research assistants and analysts who have gone on to great careers under his mentorship is deservedly legendary.
